key_insight: CVD-grown single-crystalline cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates exhibit a robust anomalous Hall effect linked to intrinsic Berry curvature and enhanced by epitaxial strain.
engineering_relevance: These non-layered ferromagnetic nanoplates offer a potential platform for spintronic devices operating above room temperature.
method: Grow epitaxial cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates by chemical vapor deposition.
Characterize crystal structure, strain, magnetism, and Hall transport.
Use density functional theory to assess strain-driven electronic reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Structural analysis finds ~4.16% interfacial compressive strain, transport shows AHE persisting well above room temperature, and DFT predicts an approximately twofold strain-induced increase in anomalous Hall conductivity consistent with experiment.
watch_item: Strain relaxes toward the surface, making thickness-dependent performance an implementation concern; SHG evidence for broken inversion symmetry remains tentative.
paper_title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge Nanoplates Grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition
